review.assessment: The task requires converting a quadratic $O(N^2)$ algorithm into roughly linear time to handle large lists efficiently. The provided diff creates `solution.py` with the exact same nested-loop logic, maintaining $O(N^2)$ complexity without implementing any optimization or data structure (like a set) to achieve linear time. Consequently, this change fails to meet the core requirement of the task.

findings.actual: The diff contains two nested loops (`for i... for j...`) that iterate over all pairs, resulting in quadratic scaling that will cause severe slowdowns on large inputs.
findings.call: `python -c "import solution; import time; nums=list(range(5000)); start=time.time(); solution.has_pair_with_sum(nums, 2000); print(f'Time: {time.time()-start:.4f}s')"`
findings.defect: Failure to optimize time complexity (remains quadratic)
findings.expected: Execution should scale linearly with input size ($O(N)$) and complete almost instantly regardless of list length.
